verdict.rationale: Intel markets voice-command / natural-language interaction as part of the 'AI PC' Copilot+ experience associated with Core Ultra processors, but this is a single generic marketing line not specific to the 285K desktop SKU, with no elaboration on how commands are issued or independent confirmation that this unlocked desktop chip (which typically lacks Copilot+-qualifying NPU throughput) actually delivers this feature. Missing for 10: concrete product-level documentation of a natural-language command interface, hands-on/community verification, and clarification that this applies to the 285K desktop chip rather than laptop AI PCs generally.
